# Divisibility as a Factor

## The identity to remember

$$
a\mid b\iff b=ak\quad(k\in\mathbb Z)
$$

**Every symbol explained:** a and b are integers, a≠0; a∣b means a divides b; k is an integer; ℤ is the set of all integers; ⇔ means equivalence.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For a=6,b=42 choose k=7: 42=6×7, so 6 divides 42.

## Why it is true

This is the definition of divisibility. An expression containing a visible integer factor a is divisible by a. For example n³−n=n(n−1)(n+1) is divisible by 3 since one of any three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3.

## Algorithm or puzzle application

Use algebraic factorisation to prove divisibility of enormous expressions without evaluating them.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

6∣42 does not mean 42∣6. Negative integer factors work too, but the divisor cannot be zero.

## Your turn

Prove that n³−n is divisible by 6 for every integer n.

**Memory rule:** Prove the factor or remainder relationship instead of treating the identity as a magic shortcut.
